messages:
jordan: Quick heads-up — I'm going to open a canary for metric_contract_v2 behind a feature flag today. This changes the per-route quota rollup field and the dashboard query shape. Need eyes on rollback and alerting.

marta: thanks — can you paste the exact FF and the read-adapter plan? want to check perf impact for console p99.

jordan: plan below. TL;DR: dual-read for 2% of traffic -> switch to v2 for 20% -> 100% if metrics look good. Quick SQL view we plan to add:

```sql
CREATE VIEW console.metric_contract_v2 AS
SELECT route_id, tenant_id, sum(tokens) AS total_tokens,
       jsonb_build_object('quota_bucket', bucket_v2) AS meta
FROM analytics.ingest_events_v2
GROUP BY route_id, tenant_id;
```

This view is behind a small read-adapter: servers will try v2 view for FF-on users; if missing, fall back to metric_contract_v1.

priya: two questions: 1) quota calc changes — will the rounding bucket change? 2) dashboards that do GROUP BY route_tag risk N+1 if we add meta jsonb; need to ensure indexes.

sam: for 1) yes, the bucket boundaries shift (we discussed earlier). We'll maintain an alias mapping so historical billing maps to v1 until full cutover. For 2) I recommend adding a partial index on (route_id, tenant_id) on ingest_events_v2, plus a gin index on meta->'quota_bucket'.

emma: Dashboard owners — heads up: chart queries that select keys from meta will need to update to meta->>'quota_bucket' or use the provided helper function `console_quota_bucket()`; otherwise they break when we switch the FF. We'll publish a migration-runbook and update the UI queries.

leo: Product note — we need to communicate to SRE and CS about a potential short dip in per-route reported QPS in the console during canary. Also decide whether alerts fire on missing metrics vs. degraded latency.

jordan: good point. Proposed alert tweaks: metric-alerts to silence missing-metric alerts for routes in the canary group for 2 hours post-rollout, but keep p95/p99 latency alerts active.

metric-alerts: automated note — we will create a suppression rule: `suppress(missing_ingest_metric) for tag:metric_contract_v2_canary for 2h`. Confirm when canary group list is published.

marta: ops checklist for canary run (short):
- [ ] Create FF entry: `metric_contract_v2.canary` (2% -> 20% -> 100%)
- [ ] Deploy read-adapter w/ staged view fallback
- [ ] Add partial index on ingest_events_v2 (route_id, tenant_id)
- [ ] Update helper functions and console query surface
- [ ] Create alert suppression rule for canary group
- [ ] Kick off a 24h job to compare v1 vs v2 aggregates and produce a diff report

sam: about the 24h drift job — I'll add a lightweight job that emits a `contract_migration_drift` telemetry event with sample size and diff_percent. Keep retention low (7d) and push to metrics-ingest for alerting.

jordan: sample telemetry event spec (so we can hook into dashboards):
```json
{ "metric": "contract_migration_drift", "route_id": "r123", "v1_total": 12345, "v2_total": 12346, "diff_pct": 0.008, "sampled": true }
```

priya: two operational concerns: 1) if the view query is slower we might blow console p50 for dashboard loads. Can we put a memcached prefix of v2 aggregates for 1hr? 2) backfill: we can't rewrite historic billing rows, so we need a compatibility mapper for billing exports.

jordan: 1) yes, read-adapter will cache results for 60min for non-realtime panels. 2) agreed — billing export will continue to pull from v1 for historical ranges; for recent ranges we add a toggle param `billing_source=v1|v2`. We'll document.

marta: rollback playbook (if things go bad):
- flip FF `metric_contract_v2.canary` -> 0%
- toggle alert suppression off
- purge memcache for the canary keys: `memcache:console:metric_contract_v2:canary:*`
- revert read-adapter flag and redeploy
- run drift report to confirm revert corrected numbers

emma: UI changes to the console: small — add a banner on dashboards showing "Using metric_contract_v2 for X% of routes" with a link to the migration doc. Also add an explicit query param `?contract=v1` for troubleshooting.

sam: one more: routing policies. If we route requests to dedicated infra for heavy queries, ensure the read-adapter respects `route_tier` and routes v2 reads to the same preferred infra. Otherwise we might mix hot/cold infra and skew cost attribution.

jordan: noted — I'll add a routing policy rule: `if FF(metric_contract_v2) then prefer infra=dedicated-telemetry` in the routing table for the canary group.

leo: timeline?

jordan: proposed timeline:
- today: FF + read-adapter deploy to staging + index creation in staging
- +48h: 2% canary in prod, start 24h drift job
- +72h: expand to 20% if drift < 0.5% and p99 latency impact < 10%
- +7d: decision to cutover to 100% or revert

marta: I'm good with that. I'll own the index migration and the suppression rule. Sam will own the drift job. Priya will review billing export docs. Emma will update UI and banner. Leo will coordinate comms with CS.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: console-read-adapter v2 -> staging at 2026-03-20T15:30Z (CI build 4891).

jordan: thanks all. I'll post the runbook link once I finish writing it. If anyone spots a dashboard that uses meta.* directly, ping me and we'll add a shallow adapter for compatibility. :thumbsup:
